Recap:
- Success criteria (from call): latency P95 < 150ms, sign-off on relevance rubric, and target cost improvements.

Proposed POC structure (high level):
1) Offline eval (1 week): Redwood runs graded offline tests on your representative dataset to validate quality and identify parameter/quantization trade-offs.
2) Online shadow (2 weeks): run requests in shadow mode against live traffic to measure latency, KV cache behavior, and production-like distributions. No customer-facing responses during shadow.
3) Controlled ramp (1 week): if shadow looks good we run a small percentage of live traffic with fallback policies.

Initial timeline (subject to dataset delivery):
- Dataset & agreed rubric: by Jan 21
- Offline eval run: Jan 24–28
- Shadow: Jan 31–Feb 11
- Ramp & handoff: Feb 14–18

Ownership:
- Redwood: infra for shadowing, model/quantization trials, evaluation harness, and rubric proposal (marissa + dylan).
- ACME: provide representative dataset, business relevance examples, and final sign-off (jared + lisa).

Next steps:

- ACME to confirm dataset readiness and point of contact by Jan 21.

— evaluation methodology (offline vs shadow) + rubric (v2)

Hi Jared / Lisa 


per Lisa's questions, outlined below is a more concrete methodology and a compact grading rubric for initial sign-off. Attached: acme-poc-eval-plan-v2.pdf, acme-poc-eval-rubric.xlsx.

1) Data needs (what ACME provides)– Representative query logs (CSV): columns: query_id, query_text, session_id, timestamp, ground_truth_id (optional)– Labeled dev set: ~1.5k queries with relevance labels (high/medium/low) 

preferred but not strictly required for the first offline pass.

2) Offline eval (purpose & deliverables)– Purpose: compare candidate model/configurations on held-out labeled set to validate quality baseline without traffic risk.– Metrics: precision@1, precision@3, nDCG@5, human-graded relevance (3-point scale).– Deliverables: offline results report, conf matrix, suggested model/config knobs.

3) Online shadow (purpose & measurement)– Purpose: measure system-level latency characteristics, cache hit behavior, and production distribution effects; opportunistically capture candidate outputs for sampling and human review.– What we will measure: P50/P95 latency, end-to-end tail, KV cache hit rate, tokens per request, error rate.– Quality checks during shadow: Redwood will sample 200 responses/day for human review and run the same scoring pipeline (where labels exist). Shadow will not return responses to end-users.

4) Grading rubric (short form for PM sign-off)– Relevance buckets: High (3), Medium (2), Low (1).– Pass condition: Offline nDCG@5 >= baseline_nDCG * 0.98 AND mean human relevance >= baseline_mean - 0.2.– Latency pass: P95 <= 150ms for shadowed samples with configured batching.

5) Ownership & timelines– Redwood: run offline tests, maintain evaluation harness, supply rubric spreadsheet (marissa + dylan).– ACME: deliver labeled set and a contact for dataset questions (Jared).– Timeline (updated): dataset confirm by Jan 21; offline run Jan 24–28; shadow Jan 31–Feb 11; weekly syncs on Fridays.

6) Next steps for this week:
- ACME: confirm dataset availability (by EOD Jan 21) and attach sample CSV to the Drive folder.
- Redwood: finalize rubric spreadsheet and provide a short sign-off deck (by Jan 22).

Attachments:
- acme-poc-eval-plan-v2.pdf (application/pdf)
- acme-poc-eval-rubric.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
